cs.t: No, thank you. I’ve recently bought a new Logitech mouse. Was using Logitech for decades, G500 series. Their software is doubtful, but was ok to “install, configure mouse and uninstall” routine. But now with Master 3S mouse I need to use Logitech Options Plus app that is terrible. Fix it first and only then roll such doubtful updates
cs.th: Logitech mouse and keyboard users are getting a free AI upgrade

cs.t: Wish there was more competition in ergonomic input devices. Was just searching for a new mouse and couldn't find a vertical mouse with acceptable reviews. Ended up forgoing the vert. mouse altogether and buying a Logitech MX Master to replace my Logitech G500 (which I've used for many years and is now discontinued) and I'm pretty happy with it so far. I'm even pleased with its gaming performance (probably not OK for highly competitive or pro gamers, but np for me). Mouse was visibly sluggish over Bluetooth but works great over Logitech RF. Although the MX Master is not billed as an ergonomic device, it fits my hand better than the G500 and I already feel some relief of the slight pain in my right wrist. I've used a Kinesis Advantage keyboard for about 3 years (and the MS Ergo 4000 for several years before that, in response to pain that developed before I even turned 20) and it's been a godsend. Would like to find a good ergo mouse before I'm forced to.
cs.th: How I stopped the RSI pain that almost destroyed my programming career

cs.t: I fully agree, and I think that's the common opinion as well. Their laptop touchpads are above all others, but I can't stand using a Magic Mouse for more than even a second. I've been using Logitech mice (G5 and later G500) for many years, and they're far more ergonomic.
cs.th: Apple's Buttonless Mouse Came From Steve Jobs' Misunderstanding
